title: Sales and business development
short: Research accounts faster and send messages that are actually relevant.
why: Most selling time goes to research, writing and follow-up. AI can prepare drafts quickly, but the value comes from relevance and accuracy, which stay with you.

tasks.name: Account research brief
tasks.what: Turn public information into a one-page brief.

tasks.name: First-touch message
tasks.what: Draft a short message tied to a public signal.
tasks.check: Remove any claim you cannot source.

tasks.name: Follow-up that adds value
tasks.what: Add something useful instead of nagging.
tasks.check: Would you want to receive it?

tasks.name: Objection handling
tasks.what: Prepare honest answers to common objections.
tasks.check: Only claim what you can back up.

tasks.name: Call preparation
tasks.what: Goal, questions, likely objections, next step.

pilot: Pick 10 accounts you would contact this week anyway.
Use the brief and first-touch prompts for 5 of them. Do the other 5 as usual.
Compare time spent and reply quality after two weeks.
metrics: Reply rate and quality of replies
risks: Pasting private customer data into a consumer account

title: Marketing and growth
short: Turn one idea into many formats without losing accuracy or brand voice.
why: Content takes time to adapt for each channel. AI is useful for first drafts and variations. Strategy, claims and brand voice remain human decisions.

tasks.name: Release to post
tasks.what: Explain a product or industry change for your audience.
tasks.check: Link every claim to its source.

tasks.name: Headline variations
tasks.what: Generate options, then choose and test.

tasks.name: Repurpose an article
tasks.what: One article into email, posts and a script.

tasks.name: Audience questions
tasks.what: What your audience searches for at each stage.

tasks.name: Brand voice check
tasks.what: Flag lines that do not sound like you.

pilot: Choose one article you already published.
Create the email and three posts with the repurpose prompt.
Publish, then compare time spent and engagement with your usual process.
risks: Generic copy that sounds like everyone else

title: Founders and business owners
short: Make decisions faster and find the repeated work worth simplifying.
why: You carry many decisions and a lot of repeated work. AI can structure your thinking and draft routine documents, but it cannot know your business context unless you provide it.

tasks.name: Pre-mortem a plan
tasks.what: Imagine it failed and list the likely reasons.

tasks.name: Weekly update
tasks.what: Turn bullets into a clear update.

tasks.name: Write an SOP
tasks.what: Turn how you do it into steps.

tasks.name: Find repeated work
tasks.what: Spot what to simplify or automate.

pilot: List last week's tasks and run the repeated-work prompt.
Pick one repeated task and write its SOP.
Trial a draft-then-review routine for two weeks and measure time saved.
metrics: Hours saved on the chosen task
Cost of tools versus time saved
risks: Sharing confidential financials or customer data

title: Students and teachers
short: Learn faster and practise better, while keeping the learning yours.
why: AI is good at explanations, practice and feedback when you stay active. It is a poor substitute for doing the thinking, and your school's rules come first.
pilot: Choose one topic you find hard.
Use explain-simply, then teach-it-back, then a practice quiz.
Check answers against your notes and record what you got wrong.
risks: Submitting AI text as your own work against school rules
Learning a confident but wrong explanation
Skipping the effort that builds understanding

title: Creators and freelancers
short: Draft faster and keep your own voice and your clients' trust.
why: Creators and freelancers sell judgement and voice. AI can speed up structure and variations, while your taste and honesty are what clients pay for.

tasks.name: Audience questions
tasks.check: Pick the ones you can answer well.

pilot: Take one finished piece and repurpose it into three formats.
Time yourself against your normal process.
Ask a client or friend which version reads better.
metrics: How often you override the draft
risks: Disclosure rules about AI use with clients or platforms
Copying phrases too close to other work

title: Developers and IT
short: Understand, test and review code faster while a person stays accountable.
why: AI can explain code, draft tests and spot risks quickly. It can also be confidently wrong, so every suggestion needs running, reading and review.

tasks.name: Debug from an error
tasks.check: Understand before you apply a fix.

pilot: Use explain, tests and review prompts on it.
Measure time to understand and the defects found, versus your usual process.
risks: Pasting secrets or proprietary code into a consumer account
